subject: Request: Deal Desk approval for immutable audit logs exception & limited discount
messages:
From: Caroline Moss <caroline.moss@axionhealth.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: procure@axionhealth.com
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Audit & retention ask for private deployment

Jonas — thanks for the productive demo last week. A couple of follow-ups from our security and compliance team: Axion is required by regulators to maintain immutable audit logs for all in-scope systems for a minimum of 24 months and retain a tamper-evident copy for audits. For a private VPC deployment we also need the ability to run third-party auditors (twice annually) against logs and to have a read-only escrow-style access path (jumpbox / Bastion) for our auditors.

We appreciate Redwood's baseline controls but this is a gating item for our procurement committee. We understand this is non-standard, so we are open to a limited, timeboxed concession while we validate controls in a pilot (e.g., 12 months initially). Also, Axion is seeking a commercial concession given the additional operational burden — aiming for guidance on available credits or a one-time implementation discount.

Attached is our security questionnaire and a short summary from our auditors. Can you loop in legal and infra so we can get a sense of feasibility and an estimated timeline/cost?

Thanks,
Caroline Moss
Director, Security & Compliance
Axion Health

Attachments: Axion_Security_Questionnaire.pdf (application/pdf)

From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Audit & retention ask for private deployment — exec / deal desk input needed

Folks — forwarding Axion's request. Key asks: 24-month immutable audit logs, third-party auditor access (read-only) via jumpbox, and a commercial concession.

My read: technically achievable but operationally non-standard. We can offer a limited, auditable solution: enable append-only/system-level logs shipped to a customer-owned S3 bucket with object lock (governance mode) for 12–24 months, and provide ephemeral, logged access for auditors via a monitored bastion. That said, this requires: a) KMS cross-account wrapping (or customer-managed CMK in their VPC), b) a scoped SLA amendment, and c) an implementation effort (~3 weeks ops + security vetting).

Asking for quick guidance on two concessions: 1) one-time implementation credit to offset engineer time (recommended: 20% of first-year committed invoice), and 2) allow temporary immutable retention for 12 months initially (Axion prefers 24) with an option to extend after pilot validation. Legal (Marissa) — any red flags with giving auditor access via jumpbox+auditing? Kimberly — need deal desk OK on the credit and exec escalations if >20%. Aditya — can infra support the S3-object-lock cross-account pattern and jumpbox for that customer?

Thanks,
Jonas
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

--- Original attachment: Axion_Security_Questionnaire.pdf

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2026 13:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Audit & retention ask for private deployment — exec / deal desk input needed

Jonas — high level legal: we can accept the model you described with strict controls and a scoped contract amendment. Conditions I'd impose: 
- Auditor access must be read-only and strictly timeboxed to scheduled windows with RBAC and session recording.
- Access requests should come through Axion's POC and be scheduled through our security operations; all sessions recorded and exports retained for Redwood audit trail.
- The customer-owned S3 with Object Lock (governance) is acceptable BUT Redwood must not assume custody liabilities: contract language should state Axion is the sole custodian of forensic logs stored in their bucket and bears responsibility for retention policies.
- No customer-managed KMS in Redwood tenant; cross-account key-wrapping (envelope encryption) preferred to avoid key custody issues.

I will prepare a narrow amendment that: 1) limits auditor access frequency (max twice/year for first 12 months), 2) sets pilot retention at 12 months, and 3) requires a mutually agreed checklist for security validation before production handover.

No absolute legal blocker, but we must not accept open-ended indemnities or permanent on-prem custody without an enterprise SOW and SOC renegotiation.

-M
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Team — I want to keep this pragmatic. Recommendation for Deal Desk approval: 
1) Approve a one-time implementation credit equal to 20% of Year 1 committed spend (cap it at a fixed $50k) to cover engineering/security uplift.
2) Offer a pilot retention period of 12 months immutable (Object Lock governance) with an optional extension to 24 months after successful security review.
3) Approve auditor access schedule: up to 2 audits in year 1, subject to Redwood Ops scheduling and recorded sessions.

If we stay within those bounds, no further executive sign-off required. If Axion insists on permanent custody or customer-managed KMS in our tenancy, escalate to execs for approval.

Kimberly Park
VP, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

Caroline — thanks for the clarity and the questionnaire. Internal review complete and we can move forward on a pilot concession: 

Summary of what Redwood can offer for a private VPC deployment (pilot):
- Immutable audit logs: export to Axion-owned S3 with AWS Object Lock (governance mode) for an initial 12-month retention period.
- Auditor access: scheduled, timeboxed read-only access via a monitored bastion (session recording + export). Max two auditor sessions in Year 1.
- Key management: envelope encryption with cross-account wrapping; Redwood will not accept custodial responsibility for customer keys inside Redwood tenancy.
- Commercial concession: one-time implementation credit equal to 20% of Year 1 committed invoice (capped at $50k).

Next steps: 
1) Caroline — confirm Axion can accept the customer-owned S3 + object-lock approach and scheduled auditor model.
2) Marissa — please prepare the narrow SLA amendment and the security checklist; we will attach to the pilot SOW.
3) Aditya — ops to provide an implementation estimate (ETA: 3 weeks from approval) and final runbook.

If Axion requires permanent custody of logs, customer-managed KMS in our tenant, or unlimited auditor access, we will need exec-level approval; current approval covers the pilot scope above.

Regards,
Jonas Weber
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

Attachments: proposed-sla-amendment-draft.pdf
